title: Finite flat modules over finite type algebras over valuation rings are finitely presented
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $M$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. If $M$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $M$ is finitely presented as a $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 053E (lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation), part (2), statement and proof at lines 5966--6001

proof.text: First $A$ is local. Indeed its fraction-field characterization [def-trf-valuation-ring] implies that any two nonzero elements $a,b\in A$ satisfy $a\mid b$ or $b\mid a$, by applying it to $a/b$. Thus its nonunits form a proper ideal: if $a,b$ are nonunits and $b=ac$, then $a+b=a(1+c)$ is a nonunit; the other divisibility and zero cases are identical, and multiplication preserves nonunits. Every proper ideal contains only nonunits, so this is the unique maximal ideal. Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and module generators $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ of $M$ over $B$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], $M$ is torsion-free over the domain $A$. Apply [lem-trf-generator-filtration-graded-module] to the chosen $b_i,m_j$. It constructs $F_dM$, the finite graded $P=A[X_0,\ldots,X_n]$-module $N=\bigoplus_dF_dM\,t^d$, and its torsion-freeness over $A$. By [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat], $N$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-graded-flat-module-finite-presentation] to $R=A$, $L=N$ and the polynomial ring $P$ with all $n+1$ weights equal to $1$. The valuation domain $A$ is nonzero and Step 1 supplies locality; Step 2 supplies the internal grading, finite generation and $A$-flatness. Thus $N$ is finitely presented over $P$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-filtered-module-evaluation-presentation] to $T_i(x)=b_ix$ and the filtration from Step 2. These maps are $A$-linear by the scalar tower and commute since $b_i(b_jx)=(b_ib_j)x=(b_jb_i)x=b_j(b_ix)$. Its increasingness, exhaustiveness and $b_iF_dM\subseteq F_{d+1}M$ are supplied there. It identifies evaluation at $t=1$ with $N/(X_0-1)N\cong M$ and evaluates a finite presentation from Step 3, proving $M$ finitely presented over $Q=A[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$. The $Q$-action is $X_ix=b_ix$.

source.place: Tag 053E(2), lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, proof: explicit filtered-polynomial homogenization followed by Tag 053C

proof.text: The map $Q\to B$, $X_i\mapsto b_i$, is surjective by the chosen algebra generators and the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Hence $B$ is a finite type $Q$-algebra, needing no extra generators [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Step 4 identifies the $Q$-action on $M$ with restriction of its given $B$-action. Apply [lem-trf-finitely-presented-over-subring] to $Q\to B$ and Step 4 to conclude that $M$ is finitely presented over $B$.
